packets.responsibility: Session registry + command surface; sequential/seek pipe-decode via bundled ffmpeg sidecar with byte-bounded cache; background bidirectional readahead; indexed MJPEG 'optimized media' transcode+random-access path; headless autobench.
packets.writer: in-process, per-session Mutex<VideoSession> fields only; filesystem writes for create_optimized_media_core (<target>/<target>.idx under temp_dir()/nemo-optimized/) and autobench_report

packets.oracle: existing #[cfg(test)] mod tests (~950 lines, ~50 tests) already exercises real behavior against the actual bundled ffmpeg binary — codec coverage, seek accuracy, tail-clamp, cache/readahead, indexed round-trip, perf-budget. Slow (spawns real ffmpeg) but authoritative and reusable as-is.
packets.notes: ENTANGLEMENT ANALYSIS (why kept as one packet, not further split): sub-responsibilities (pipe engine / readahead / indexed path) all mutate the same VideoSession struct behind the same per-session lock, dispatched from one function (decode_frame_core). spawn_readahead and decode_at share and race on proc/cache directly — not viable to split readahead from the pipe engine without a code change first (out of scope for a read-only census). The indexed path is the least entangled and is the best candidate for a *future* intra-file refactor (e.g. an enum splitting VideoSession by engine) before any real file split. Paired 1:1 with C05.native-video.decode-session across the JS/Rust boundary — must move together. Carries DEF-15, DEF-16, DEF-17, DEF-18 (all below); DEF-15 (stale GPL/LGPL doc) should be reconciled before this packet's module header is used as a licensing rationale in any extraction doc.

cross_cutting_notes: Export-format parity gap (spans C05.export.frame-compositor / lottie-bodymovin / rive-mcp): the engine-routing gate (exportNeedsEngine and its sub-predicates) exists only to route RASTER export through the Rust engine for effects/blend-matte/3D/motion-blur/keyed-order/image-mesh/vector-brush-centerline-motion. Lottie and Rive exporters never consult these gates at all and always read baked per-frame stroke dicts — so those features are silently wrong or missing in Lottie/Rive output, beyond the handful of gaps (blend modes, draw order) the files already self-admit in their own header comments. This is the same 'one reader/consumer updated, others left behind' shape as CLAUDE.md §1's family-of-bug-#1, here across export formats rather than across layer.children readers. Recommend either (a) a single export feature-parity checklist/test all three exporters must satisfy, or (b) an explicit, documented decision that Lottie/Rive stay second-class for engine-only features.

Two independent importers (figma-import.js, psd-import-bridge.js) both create a new layer via createUserLayer and call saveActiveLayerFrame() without ever calling ensureKeyframe() or checking state.currentFrame (DEF-5, DEF-6). svg-import.js, which only ever inserts into the *existing* active layer, does not have this bug. This is CLAUDE.md §1's family-of-bug-#1 pattern occurring twice, independently, in sibling files — worth flagging as a systemic gap (missing shared 'create-layer-and-persist' helper that always keyframes) rather than two unrelated one-off bugs.

Two files (linked-media.js, native-video-bridge.js) both mutate state.mediaLibrary entry fields directly instead of going through media-library.js's own updateEntry() API (DEF-12). This is a pre-existing cross-file write-boundary violation that blocks media-library.js from being extracted as a self-contained module with a real write boundary until fixed.

svg-import.js's explodeLeaf (boolean-result explosion) and tools.js's insertBooleanResult are two independent implementations of overlapping logic that must be kept in sync by hand (DEF-8) — same hazard class as CLAUDE.md §3's Rust dual-function warning, here in JS.

video_decode.rs's own top-of-file doc comment (GPL rationale) contradicts its own test-module comment (LGPL) and both are stale relative to CLAUDE.md §7's dated 2026-08-18 LGPL rebuild record (DEF-15) — a documentation-accuracy issue, not a licensing violation (the actual shipped binary is already correctly LGPL per CLAUDE.md), but worth a follow-up doc-only correction before this file's header is cited as licensing evidence.

known_defects.summary: lottieBuild's stroke filter omits !sd.elemHidden (present in exportBuildFrame:78) — a per-element 'eye'-hidden element is excluded from PNG/video/GIF/MP4 export but not from Lottie export.

exportHasLayerCompositing / exportBuildFrame's whole compositing loop never checks isMask/maskMode (lottieBuild does exclude isMask at :1115) — a project using only in-layer masks falls through the plain-Paper raster path and paints the mask shape as an ordinary opaque shape instead of excluding/clipping it.
Per-frame stroke gathering never calls SMGroup.applyCombinesToStrokes (present in export.js:91 and :1118) — non-destructive combine groups silently do not apply to Rive export.

Lottie and Rive exporters never consult exportNeedsEngine or any of its sub-predicates — 3D layers, Motion Blur, keyed Order, and Image Mesh are silently wrong/missing in those two export formats, undocumented beyond the blend-mode/draw-order gaps the files already self-admit.

createUserLayer marks only frame 0 as a keyframe; figma-import.js never calls ensureKeyframe() or checks state.currentFrame, so importing while parked on any frame != 0 makes saveActiveLayerFrame() silently no-op — content renders once then vanishes on next frame nav/undo/reload.
Same missing-ensureKeyframe/currentFrame-check bug as DEF-5.

Raster.onError resolves identically to onLoad, so a failed image fetch/decode still increments report.imagesImported and is never reported as skipped; the half-built Raster stays inserted in the layer.

explodeLeaf duplicates insertBooleanResult's (tools.js:6967) exterior/hole classification instead of reusing it, deliberately, to preserve real bezier handles/per-shape style — the two must be manually kept in sync going forward.

duplicateLayer shares _nvSessionId by value between two layer objects (timeline.js:1221,1296, self-documented as intentional), but _optimizeLayerMedia/_relinkWebVideo/replaceNativeVideoSource each unconditionally close(oldSession) with no check for another layer still holding that id — the sibling's video freezes silently (console.error only) on its next frame sync.

Layer deletion (app.js:3432, app.js:5104, timeline.js:1050) splices a nativeVideo layer out of state without ever calling SMNativeVideo.close() — the ffmpeg child process (desktop) or fully-buffered demuxed sample array (web) leaks for the rest of the app session.
removeEntry/cleanupOrphans drop the catalog entry (the app's only pointer to m.webHandleId) without calling linked-media.js's forgetHandle() — orphans the IndexedDB linkedHandle record permanently.

linked-media.js (:148,154,371,391) and native-video-bridge.js (:794,800,1368,1370,1410) mutate state.mediaLibrary entry fields directly instead of going through media-library.js's updateEntry() API, then manually call reload(). Works today but blocks media-library.js from having a real, closed write boundary.
resolveSrcLayer (media-library.js:92-99) and _resolveEntryLayer (linked-media.js:347-351) are independent, near-identical 'layerUid, else layerName' resolvers.

fetch_google_font takes only the first url(...) in Google's CSS2 response; the endpoint commonly returns multiple @font-face blocks scoped to different unicode-range subsets (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, vietnamese...), so the returned font file can have incomplete glyph coverage for non-Latin text.

Top-of-file doc still asserts the bundled ffmpeg sidecar is GPL (--enable-gpl --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265), contradicting the test module's own comment 1500+ lines later ('the bundled LGPL sidecar is the default') and CLAUDE.md §7's dated 2026-08-18 LGPL rebuild record. Documentation-accuracy issue only — the shipped binary is already correctly LGPL.
known_defects.severity: doc-only, follow-up recommended before citing as licensing evidence

No session reaper/TTL: if JS never calls close_video_session (reload/crash), the VideoSessions entry and its child ffmpeg/converter processes are never reclaimed until the whole app process exits.
optimized_media_target keys its cache on path+size+mtime-in-seconds; a same-second rewrite of identical size can false-hit a stale transcode.
